newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt warns of danger of Israel housing decision.
newsitem.headline: Egypt warns of danger of Israel housing decision.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Thursday said Israel's decision to build homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem could lead to an outbreak of violence between Palestinians and Israelis.

Israel's approval on Wednesday of a plan to build 6,500 houses in Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa has sparked criticism from its key ally the United States and Palestinian warnings that it could unleash bloodshed.

"The situation is dangerous and I warn of a deterioration of this situation and of increased difficulties for the peace process," Mubarak told reporters on a trip to the Mediterranean town of Mersa Matrouh.
"Public opinion must be taken into account before any decision is taken and negotiations must be resorted to without imposing de facto reality," he added.
Mubarak said he told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a telephone conversation on Wednesday not to take any decision about Jerusalem without first consulting Palestinians.
"I told Netanyahu that I was worried about the consequences of building a new settlement in Jerusalem and of the outbreak of violence because of this," Mubarak said.
The telephone conversation took place before an Israeli ministerial committee gave the green light to the construction.
Mubarak said he would meet Netanyahu but did not say when.
Egypt became the first Arab state to make peace with Israel in 1979 but relations between the two countries have cooled since the election of the right wing Netanyahu last year.
Egypt has been particularly critical of his policy on building or expanding settlements on occupied Arab land.
The Cairo-based Arab League said on Thursday it would hold an emergency meeting of its permanent representatives on Sunday to discuss the Israeli decision.
Arab League spokesman Tala'at Hamen told Reuters the Palestinian Authority representative had requested the meeting after Israel approved on Wednesday the building of the houses.
Israel says all of Jerusalem is its capital. Palestinians consider Arab East Jerusalem, which Israel seized during the 1967 Middle East war, the capital of a future Palestinian state.
